name: pyupgrade-b01874bf-blind20-v2-ots
instr:
# pyupgrade rewrites come out wrong across many fixers — diagnosing without a test suite

I run this source-rewriting tool over a lot of code and after picking up the current checkout an alarming amount of it misbehaves. Some rewrites silently stop happening, some produce garbled source, some now touch code they used to leave alone, and a few blow up outright. The repository has received 20 separate undocumented edits. Below is everything I have been able to pin down, grouped by the kind of rewrite.

## six compatibility rewrites

- When one of six's string/text type aliases is used as the type argument of an `isinstance(...)` or `issubclass(...)` check, it is no longer replaced by the plain builtin name: I expect `isinstance(s, str)` / `issubclass(tp, str)` back and I get something else. This holds regardless of the whitespace around the attribute access. Other simple six attribute replacements still come back correct.
- Classes declared through six's `with_metaclass` helper are no longer converted to the `metaclass=` keyword form. Every shape of it is wrong now: a lone metaclass argument, a metaclass plus one or several bases, a version with a trailing comma, the helper accessed through the module or imported by name, odd spacing, and the variant where a redundant `object` base should be elided. Other six-related class rewrites still behave.
